subject.title: Tailscale permission error for openclaw user

question: Should the installer automatically grant `{{ openclaw_user }}` as the Tailscale operator for serve mode, and what should happen when another operator is already configured?
rationale: The source-level fix is clear, but the permanent behavior changes who can manage Tailscale Serve configuration and may overwrite an existing host preference; that is a maintainer security-boundary decision, not only a mechanical Ansible edit.

options.title: Approve a guarded operator grant
options.body: Set the OpenClaw service user as operator only when safe, preserve or fail clearly on a different existing operator, and keep auth-key commands redacted; this best matches the reported serve-mode need.

options.title: Keep operator setup manual
options.body: Document the `tailscale set --operator` requirement and avoid changing host Tailscale authority from the installer, leaving serve mode dependent on an operator-run command.

options.title: Split auth-key from operator policy
options.body: Land a narrower auth-key/BackendState fix while keeping the serve-mode operator decision open for a separate security review.

recommendation.title: Approve a guarded operator grant
recommendation.body: Set the OpenClaw service user as operator only when safe, preserve or fail clearly on a different existing operator, and keep auth-key commands redacted; this best matches the reported serve-mode need.

likelyOwner.reason: The central unresolved choice is the scoped sudo/Tailscale permission boundary, and history ties that area most directly to alauppe.
